To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the probability distribution of the steady state of a driven system is independent of the details of the thermal bath when (ii) the period of the external field is short and (iii) all relevant Hamiltonians commute with each other.
a periodically driven open system reaches a steady state whose probability distribution is independent from the detailed nature of a thermal bath, and is described by the Floquet Gibbs distribution.

the Floquet-Gibs state emerges in the periodically driven open systems under the conditions that the Hamiltonian of relevant system is bounded, the period of the external driving field is short and the Hamiltonian of interaction between the system and thermal bath commutes with the Hamiltonian of driving field.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the steady state of a system driven by a periodic external field coupled to a thermal reservoir.
the steady-state properties of a periodically driven quantum system in the weak coupling to the thermal bath.
a general condition for emergence of the steady state of a Floquet-Gibbes state, which is independent of the nature of the thermal baths.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, in the presence of the conditions (i), (ii), and (iii), the probability distribution of the steady state is independent of the thermal bath and is described by the Floquet-Gilbert distribution.
the steady state of the periodically driven open system is the Floquet-Gibsbs distribution if the above three conditions are satisfied.
the steady-state distribution is given by the Gibbs distribution for the Floquet states at the bath temperature when the Hamiltonians of all relevant systems and the interaction Hamiltonian commute.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Floquet-Ginsburg-Landau state is realized in the periodically driven open system.
a Floquet-Gibb state emerges in a periodically driven system when the system is coupled to a thermal reservoir.
the Floquet-Gibs state emerges in a periodically driven open system when the driving field is strong and the system is weakly coupled to the thermal bath.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Floquet-Ginsburg state can emerge in the periodically driven open quantum systems even when the external fields are strong.
the emergence of the Floquent-Gibbs state does not depend on the details of the driving field or the thermal bath, but is determined only by the properties of the relevant system.
the steady state of a weakly coupled system can be described by a Floquet-Gibb state, even when the system is strongly driven.
